examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'classics' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We are a classic French restaurant.

examples.text: А классика никогда не уходит из моды.
examples.trans: And classics never go out of fashion.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('classic, classical').

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень классический день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very classic day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Container. Common feminine noun meaning 'box, carton' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We were putting it into boxes.
A big box was standing on the floor.

examples.text: Шалфей был. Мы его в коробки клали.
examples.trans: It was sage. We were putting it into boxes.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'beauty' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'little chicken, darling' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть курочка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always little chicken.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fashion, habit' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Look at the habit he picked up!

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая мода.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new fashion.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fashionable, trendy, stylish').

examples.trans: This is a trendy open kitchen format.

examples.text: Это очень модный формат открытой кухни в Москве.
examples.trans: This is a very trendy open-kitchen format in Moscow.

examples.text: Нагиев пришёл в ресторан в новом модном костюме.
examples.trans: Nagiyev came to the restaurant in a new fashionable suit.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Usually singular collective. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'орудование'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'equipment, machinery' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это договор на покупку строительного оборудования.
examples.trans: This is a contract for the purchase of construction equipment.
New equipment was delivered to the factory.

examples.text: А что у меня из оборудования?
examples.trans: And what equipment do I have?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.en: to get tired, to be tired
meanings.note: Russian past 'я устал(а)' = English 'I'm tired'

examples.trans: She is very tired after work.

examples.text: Самсон, я устал. Мне сегодня ещё в суд идти!
examples.trans: Samson, I'm tired. I still have to go to court today!

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Уходи! = Go away!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.

Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

Predicative or adverb. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
